stories.delivered_paragraph: Spotify added 1 million more premium subscribers than it had forecast in the second quarter, helping it deliver €4.777 billion in revenue, up 14%, even as total monthly-user growth slightly missed guidance. The results suggest Spotify’s push into new features is supporting profitability as it balances growth with higher technology spending.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The White House does not plan to publicly release its new voluntary framework for evaluating advanced AI models, Axios reported, citing three people familiar with the discussions. Officials briefed industry staff on the completed framework, but companies not included, outside researchers, policymakers and U.S. allies may not know its contents or which “trusted partners” get early model access. The secrecy could complicate international coordination on AI security as cyber threats and competition from Chinese developers intensify.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Sony Music has promoted longtime in-house lawyer Stephanie Yu to general counsel and executive vice president for business and legal affairs, replacing Julie Swidler after her departure. Yu joined Sony in 2005 and will oversee its legal, business and government-affairs work while reporting to chairman Rob Stringer and COO Kevin Kelleher. She takes over a consequential role after Swidler’s 18-year tenure, as music companies navigate licensing, distribution, acquisitions and policy disputes.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Waymo has removed the waitlist for its robotaxi service in Dallas, allowing the public to request rides as the company expands its self-driving operations. The move makes Dallas the latest test of whether Waymo can turn limited deployments into broadly available transport service. It also advances the Alphabet-owned company’s wider effort to scale in the United States, Britain and Europe, where regulation, safety oversight and operational reliability will determine how quickly driverless rides can grow.

The trend points to housing costs and social connection creating unusual shared-living models across age groups.

stories.delivered_paragraph: President Volodymyr Zelensky shared video showing a Russian drone pursuing a street vendor in Ukraine’s Kherson region before exploding near him; a doctor said the man survived with shrapnel wounds, concussion and trauma. Ukrainian officials called the attack a deliberate assault on a civilian and part of what they describe as “human safari” drone attacks in front-line areas. The footage adds to evidence Ukraine is seeking to publicize of the civilian danger posed by cheap, remotely operated weapons.

stories.delivered_paragraph: French rescuers brought 173 migrants ashore at Boulogne-sur-Mer after the engine of their Channel-crossing boat caught fire, with 11 people suffering minor injuries. The vessel left France on Monday night, and authorities said some passengers had initially refused assistance while trying to reach the UK; prosecutors have opened an investigation and detained an Egyptian national. The incident underscores the continued danger of small-boat crossings despite British and French efforts to disrupt smuggling networks.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Leonardo DiCaprio’s Re:wild and the Bezos Earth Fund have launched the $200 million Phoenix Species Project to help recover 100 species facing imminent extinction. The effort will support mammals, amphibians, reptiles, birds, fish, invertebrates and plants in 30 countries, across habitats from oceans to volcanic plains. By targeting species judged closest to extinction, the fund aims to direct private conservation money toward recoveries where delays could make losses irreversible.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The European Union praised Spain’s response after a surge of migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco, with Madrid saying it has returned about 70,000 of the 72,000 people who arrived illegally last week. Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on North Africa’s Mediterranean coast, is a recurring flashpoint in European migration policy because of its border with Morocco. The scale and rapid returns will likely sharpen scrutiny of border enforcement and Spain’s cooperation with Morocco.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Writers Guild of America will hold its 79th annual awards on February 13, 2027, at the Edison Ballroom in New York and the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles, with nominations due to be announced January 8. The dates give studios and contenders an early marker in the next awards-season calendar.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Science creator Hank Green said he is stepping back from production after criticism of his AI use, describing his reliance on large language models as “not healthy” even though he said he used them to find research sources rather than write scripts. The episode has focused attention on a poorly understood middle ground between ordinary chatbot use and severe cases involving delusions or psychiatric harm. It raises questions about dependence, credibility and how creators disclose AI’s role in their work.

stories.delivered_paragraph: OpenAI drew backlash after influencers posted from its first apparent brand trip, a “Summer Club” retreat outside New York featuring cabins, branded merchandise and monogrammed pajamas. The event followed a familiar consumer-brand marketing model, but critics questioned why an AI company facing debates over copyright, accuracy and social effects was promoting itself through luxury influencer content. The reaction shows how OpenAI’s consumer marketing can collide with public expectations that it address the technology’s broader risks.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Oil prices fell more than 5% after U.S. officials said talks with Iran had progressed toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz, sending Brent crude below $80 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate to $76. Both benchmarks reached their lowest levels since July 13 as traders priced in the possible return of disrupted shipments, though Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was no final deal. The decline could ease fuel-price pressure, but previous failed negotiations have kept the market volatile.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said the central bank’s 3.5%-3.75% policy-rate target is sufficiently restrictive to bring inflation back toward 2%, while stressing she remains open-minded about future moves. Her comments reinforce the Fed’s cautious stance as officials wait for clearer evidence that inflation is slowing.
